mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X6 30d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW X6 30d engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£4,500 supply-only for a rebuilt M57D30, N57D30A or B57D30A unit, or £3,800-£6,500 fitted by a specialist. Used M57D30 engines: £800-£1,500 depending on mileage and condition. Used N57D30A engines: £1,000-£1,800. Used B57D30A/B engines: £1,800-£3,000. Professional fitting adds £1,000-£2,000 to the engine cost.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X6 30d engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 30d engine has evolved across three generations. The M57D30 is considered the most robust, regularly exceeding 200,000 miles with proper maintenance. The N57D30A introduced rear-mounted timing chain issues - the most common catastrophic failure between 80,000-120,000 miles. The B57D30A/B in G06 models has resolved the timing chain concerns but can suffer from EGR cooler and AdBlue system issues. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 miles) are critical for all variants.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW X6 30d N57?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of N57 timing chain failure in the X6 30d are: cold-start rattle that disappears as the engine warms - the primary early warning; rattling or slapping noise from the rear of the engine, especially during startup or acceleration; decreased power, acceleration problems, or sluggish performance; complete engine seizure with no warning - some owners report failure without any prior symptoms.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage BMW X6 30d?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an E71 X6 30d worth £8,000-£12,000, a £3,800-£6,500 rebuilt engine can make financial sense if the body, gearbox, and interior are in good condition. For an F16 30d worth £12,000-£20,000, replacement is more comfortably viable. For a G06 30d worth £25,000+, replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to approximately 60-70% of the car's value. E71 30ds with rust-free bodies and good gearboxes are worth saving. F16 30ds with N57 timing chain failure are often worth rebuilding given their higher residual values. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: What causes the BMW X6 30d EGR cooler to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: EGR cooler failure in the X6 30d is typically caused by internal cracking due to thermal stress, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust system. Symptoms include coolant disappearing without obvious leaks, white exhaust smoke, overheating, and rough idle. BMW has issued recalls for EGR cooler defects on diesel models, citing potential fire risk. Replacement at a specialist costs £550-£850. A permanent fix option is available via EGR cooler delete kits for off-road use.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW X6 30d engine with a different engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective for the X6 30d. The M57D30, N57D30A, and B57D30A/B are the only engines fitted to the 30d from the factory - stick to like-for-like replacement. Swapping to a 40d requires different ECU, wiring, and turbo system. Swapping between generations (e.g. N57 to B57) is not feasible due to different platforms and electronics. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Our marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X6 30d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X6 30d arrived with the E71 in 2008 as the entry-level diesel for BMW's Sports Activity Coupé. It has remained the core diesel choice across all three generations, evolving from the M57 through the N57 to the current B57 mild-hybrid unit - always delivering effortless torque and strong motorway economy.

milestones.description: BMW X6 30d (E71) launches with the M57D30 3.0-litre straight-six diesel, producing 235hp and 520Nm
E71 LCI introduces the N57D30A engine with common-rail injection, producing 245hp
F16 X6 30d debuts with the N57D30A producing 258hp and 560Nm
B57D30A engine introduced in F16 models, featuring revised timing chain design and improved emissions
G06 X6 30d arrives with the B57D30A/B featuring 48V mild hybrid technology and up to 286hp

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW X6 30d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW X6 30d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X6 30d is powered by a 3.0-litre straight-six diesel - the M57D30 (E71, 2008-2010), N57D30A (E71 LCI and F16 early, 2010-2015), or the B57D30A/B (F16 late and G06, 2015-present). The N57's rear-mounted timing chain is the most common catastrophic failure point driving replacement demand for E71 and early F16 30d owners. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N57 Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW X6 30d N57D30A Fails
problems.rootCause: The N57 engine places the timing chain at the rear of the engine block. Chain tensioner wear allows slack to develop, causing guide breakage. If ignored, the chain can snap, allowing pistons to contact valves - catastrophic engine failure requiring full replacement. The rattling noise typically originates from the rear of the engine, and some owners report failure with no warning symptoms at all.

repairOptions.tier: Preventative - timing chain & tensioner replacement (catch early rattle)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets. Engine remains in vehicle.
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000-100,000 miles. Only viable if chain has not jumped or snapped.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt N57D30A engine with upgraded chain components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has snapped causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW X6 30d in the UK is worth between £8,000 and £35,000 depending on generation, condition, and mileage. On an E71 30d worth £8,000-£12,000, a £3,800-£6,500 rebuilt engine represents a significant portion of the vehicle's value - evaluate body and gearbox condition carefully. On an F16 30d worth £12,000-£20,000, replacement is more comfortably viable. On a G06 30d worth £25,000+, replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your N57-powered X6 30d develops a cold-start rattle that disappears as the engine warms, act immediately - preventative chain replacement saves thousands. Once the chain snaps, the engine is beyond economic repair. For an F16 30d, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components represents better value than dealer replacement. For a lower-value E71, consider whether the rest of the vehicle justifies the investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N57D30A BMW X6 30d engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler & Injector Seal Failure - Why the BMW X6 30d Loses Coolant and Runs Rough
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop internal cracks due to thermal stress, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust system - causing white smoke, rapid coolant loss, and potentially a fire risk. Injector seals degrade over time, allowing diesel to contaminate the engine oil, thinning it and destroying bearings.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed EGR cooler, flush cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught immediately after coolant loss noticed

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - injector seal replacement & oil change
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, replace all copper seals, full oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before bearing damage - check for diesel smell on dipstick

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine (overheated / bearing failure)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new EGR cooler and injectors, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if engine was driven after coolant loss or diesel contamination caused knocking

problems.recommendation: EGR cooler failure gives warning signs - coolant loss and white smoke - before engine damage occurs. Stop driving immediately and replace the cooler at a specialist for under £850. BMW has issued recalls for EGR cooler defects on diesel models. Similarly, the smell of diesel on the dipstick is the early warning for injector seal failure - catch it before the bottom end begins knocking. On any 30d approaching 100,000 miles, have both the EGR cooler and injector seals inspected.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW X6 30d engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Blockage & Regeneration Failure - Why the BMW X6 30d Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: BMW X6 30d (all variants, especially urban-only cars)
problems.rootCause: Repeated short journeys prevent passive DPF regeneration. Ash builds up beyond the ECU's ability to force-regenerate. Eventually, back pressure damages the turbo, cracks the exhaust manifold, or causes engine oil dilution from failed regeneration attempts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic forced regeneration, motorway test drive, differential pressure sensor check
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary - works only if ash load is below 80%

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF, flow bench clean to factory spec, replace pressure sensor, regen
repairOptions.longevity: 40,000-60,000 miles - effective but not permanent on high-mileage cars

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New DPF (genuine or high-quality aftermarket), turbo inspection/rebuild, oil change, regen
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent for DPF - turbo longevity depends on damage severity

problems.recommendation: If your X6 30d is a town car doing under 15,000 miles per year, a DPF cleaning every 2-3 years is cheaper than an engine replacement. Once you see "Drivetrain malfunction - continued driving possible", get a forced regeneration immediately - ignoring it will kill the turbo. On an X6 30d worth under £10,000, a £450-£750 cleaning is sensible; over £10,000, consider a new DPF if you plan to keep the car for 3+ years. Never buy an X6 diesel that has done only urban miles without a DPF ash report.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW X6 30d DPF cleaning and replacement quotes
